## Data Acquisition

### State Electricity Profiles

```{r}
#| label: eia-sep-download
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(fs)
library(gt)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

## Data Acquisition - NTD Energy Usage

```{r}
#| label: ntd-energy-download
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```
the description column was dropped from the calculation because it describes the fuel rather than measuring it.

```{r}
#| label: ntd-service-download
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Data Cleaning and Preparation

### Recoding Transit Modes

```{r}
#| label: recode-mode
# Translate NTD two-letter mode codes into readable names.
# Defined once as a function so both NTD tables are recoded identically.
recode_mode <- function(x) {
  recode_values(x,
    "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
    "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
    "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
    "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
    "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
    "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
    "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
    "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
    "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
    "MB" ~ "Bus",
    "MG" ~ "Monorail / Automated Guideway",
    "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
    "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
    "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
    "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
    "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
    default = "Unknown"
  )
}

NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(mode = recode_mode(mode))
```


```{r}
#| label: recode-mode-energy
NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(Mode = recode_mode(Mode))
```

## Exploring the Data

### State Electricity Profiles

#### Most Expensive Electricity

```{r}
#| label: fig-expensive-electricity
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = electricity_price_MWh,
    y = fct_reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh)
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7a4b", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::dollar(electricity_price_MWh)),
    hjust = -0.15, size = 4.5
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "Five Most Expensive States for Retail Electricity",
    x       = "Average retail price per MWh",
    y       = NULL,
    caption = "Source: US Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```


#### National Average Emissions

##### The Calculation

```{r}
#| label: us-avg-co2
# Weight each state's emissions rate by how much electricity it generates
us_avg_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  summarize(avg = weighted.mean(CO2_MWh, w = generation_MWh)) |>
  pull(avg)

# Unweighted average, for comparison
us_simple_avg_co2 <- mean(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh)
```

The average CO₂ emissions rate from US electricity generation, weighted by how much electricity each state produces, was `r scales::comma(us_avg_co2, accuracy = 1)` pounds of CO₂ per MWh. This means that the average emissions rate reflects the electricity generated across the country rather than treating every state equally. Compared with the cleanest and dirtiest states in the dataset, this national average provides a useful benchmark for understanding differences in electricity-related emissions.

#### Rarest Energy Sources

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rarest-sources
# Find the 3 primary sources used by the fewest states
rarest_sources <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  count(primary_source) |>
  slice_min(n, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(primary_source)

EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  filter(primary_source %in% rarest_sources) |>
  group_by(primary_source) |>
  summarize(
    n_states  = n(),
    states    = paste(sort(state), collapse = ", "),
    avg_price = mean(electricity_price_MWh)
  ) |>
  arrange(n_states) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    primary_source = "Primary Source",
    n_states       = "Number of States",
    states         = "States",
    avg_price      = "Avg. Retail Price (per MWh)"
  ) |>
  fmt_currency(columns = avg_price, currency = "USD") |>
  tab_header(title = "The Three Rarest Primary Energy Sources") |>
  tab_source_note("Source: US Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles")
```

#### Texas vs. New York

```{r}
#| label: tx-vs-ny
tx_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
ny_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY") |> pull(CO2_MWh)

# How many times more CO2 Texas emits per MWh than New York
tx_ny_ratio <- tx_co2 / ny_co2
```

Texas produces `r round(tx_ny_ratio, 1)` times as much CO₂ per MWh of electricity as New York. This means New York's electricity generation is substantially cleaner than Texas's.

### Transit Service
#### Busiest Transit Services

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-upt
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
NTD_SERVICE |>
  # Combine directly operated + purchased service for each agency + mode
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, mode) |>
  summarize(total_upt = sum(total_upt), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total_upt, n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    # Shorten names like "King County, dba: King County Metro"
    agency_short = str_remove(AGENCY, ".*dba:\\s*"),
    label        = str_glue("{agency_short} ({city}): {mode}")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = total_upt, y = fct_reorder(label, total_upt))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7a4b", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::label_number(
      scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale(),
      accuracy  = 0.1
    )(total_upt)),

  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),

  labs(
```

#### States with the Least Transit Travel

```{r}
#| label: fig-fewest-miles
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
# Passenger miles by state (50 states only), tracking how many
# services actually reported miles. Smaller "Reduced" and "Rural"
# reporters are not required to report passenger miles.
miles_by_state <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(state %in% state.abb) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(
    total_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_reported  = sum(!is.na(sum_passenger_miles)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(state_name = state.name[match(state, state.abb)])

# States where no agency reported passenger miles
no_miles_states <- miles_by_state |>
  filter(n_reported == 0) |>
  pull(state_name)

miles_by_state |>
  filter(n_reported > 0) |>
  slice_min(total_miles, n = 5) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = total_miles,
    y = reorder(state_name, -total_miles)

  geom_col(fill = "#b5651d", width = 0.7) +
```

#### State Coverage

```{r}
#| label: state-coverage
# 50 states with no transit service in the NTD data
missing_states <- state.name[!state.abb %in% NTD_SERVICE$state]

# Regions in the NTD data that are not one of the 50 states (DC, territories)
extra_regions <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  distinct(state) |>
  filter(!state %in% state.abb) |>
  pull(state) |>
  sort()

# Readable names for the non-state regions
region_names <- c(
  AS = "American Samoa", DC = "District of Columbia", GU = "Guam",
  MP = "Northern Mariana Islands", PR = "Puerto Rico", VI = "US Virgin Islands"
)
extra_region_names <- unname(region_names[extra_regions])
```

The NTD data cover all 50 states and include `r length(extra_regions)` additional regions: `r str_flatten_comma(extra_region_names)`. However, these regions will be excluded from the emissions analysis because the EIA dataset covers only the 50 states.

## Data Analysis
## Calculating Emissions
### Preparing Service Data

```{r}
#| label: service-agg
# Collapse service to one row per agency + mode
# (combining directly operated and purchased transportation)
SERVICE_AGG <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state, uza_name, mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt      = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_miles    = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    miles_reported = any(!is.na(sum_passenger_miles)),
    any_flagged    = any(flagged_likely_inaccurate),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Combining the Data

```{r}
#| label: combine-data
# Energy: match the service table's ID format ("00001") and column names
ENERGY_CLEAN <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = sprintf("%05d", as.integer(`NTD ID`))) |>
  select(-`NTD ID`, -`Agency Name`, -`Bio-Diesel Description`) |>
  rename(mode = Mode)

# EIA: keep only what the emissions calculation needs
EIA_CO2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh)

# One row per agency + mode with service, fuel use, and grid emissions
EMISSIONS_BASE <- SERVICE_AGG |>
  inner_join(ENERGY_CLEAN,
             join_by(NTD_ID, mode),
             relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(EIA_CO2,
             join_by(state == abbreviation),
             relationship = "many-to-one")
```
